Sir Edward Charles Buck (1838 - 1916) was a senior British civil servant in India and a leading figure in agricultural reform. He served as Secretary to the Revenue and Agricultural Department and was known for supporting Indian arts and rural industry. Buck was knighted in 1886 and made Knight Commander of the Star of India in 1897.
Franz Reuleaux (1829 - 1905) was a German mechanical engineer and a leading theorist of kinematics. He served as director of the Berlin Technical Academy and represented Germany at numerous international exhibitions. He is best known for the Reuleaux triangle and for advancing the study of machine motion.

McCrea Hazlett (1916 - 2007) was an accomplished educator and American diplomat. His many accolades included serving as Provost and Vice-President, University of Rochester; Director, the Rochester Arts Council and Professor Emeritus of English, University of Rochester. His academic specialties included English literature of the 17th century and the art, literature and culture of India. He was the first Director of the American Institute of Indian Studies, Pune, India. In 1971, Hazlett was appointed cultural affairs officer to the U.S. Embassy in New Delhi.

Sita de Silva (1935 - 2018) served as the founding Secretary of the George Keyt Foundation from its establishment in June 1988. Together with her husband Cedric, the Foundationâs founding Chairman, she helped launch and manage major annual programmes such as the Kala Pola art fair, the Young Contemporaries exhibition and numerous other events that provided vital exposure for Sri Lankan artists. Visionaries in their own right, the de Silvas worked tirelessly to promote and preserve the legacy of their friend George Keyt, and are widely remembered for their enduring contribution to the development of modern and contemporary Sri Lankan art.
